description:
FOUND s493 by the one-liner battery (noted in #2097 as "List::Util max on non-numeric strings returns
the first of equals, perl the last"), FILED s506f (Opus, 2026-10-04) because no task carried it.

REPRODUCER (perl 5.40.3 vs PCL):
  perl -MList::Util=max -e 'print max("The","quick","dog"), " ", max("a","b"), "\n"'   -> dog b
  pcl  -MList::Util=max -e 'print max("The","quick","dog"), " ", max("a","b"), "\n"'   -> The a
  (min("a","b") is "a" in both)
Battery row ol-052: `perl -MList::Util=max -alne 'print max @F'`.

Probe perl's XS (ListUtil.xs min/max: the `magic` / numeric-compare path; with every value numifying
to 0 it keeps replacing on `>=`?) before fixing lib/List/Util.pm -- the shim is the right layer
(rule 9a).
subject: List::Util max over strings that numify EQUAL returns a different element than perl's XS max (`max("a","b")`: perl "b", PCL "a")
